paragraphs.source_en: Oda Uraku, together with Oda Nobukatsu's senior retainers Takigawa Katsutoshi and Hijikata Katsuhisa, came to the Tokugawa as Nobukatsu's envoys. They had not been dispatched by Toyotomi Hideyoshi; rather, Nobukatsu had sent them at Hideyoshi's command.

units.source_en: Oda Uraku, together with Oda Nobukatsu's senior retainers Takigawa Katsutoshi and Hijikata Katsuhisa, came to the Tokugawa as Nobukatsu's envoys. They had not been dispatched by Toyotomi Hideyoshi; rather, Nobukatsu had sent them at Hideyoshi's command.

paragraphs.source_en: When Tokugawa Ieyasu saw that even Uraku, one of Hideyoshi's confidants, had come, he made a special journey from Okazaki back to Hamamatsu to receive the envoys. By then, Nishio Castle's coastal defenses had been redeployed, and the reconstruction of Okazaki was under way. In deploying his forces and governing his domains, Ieyasu adopted the mobile, flexible system used in Kai and appointed Honda Sakuzaemon castellan of Okazaki. Only then had Okazaki finally settled the turmoil caused by Kazumasa's flight.

paragraphs.source_en: On the twenty-first day of the first month of Tenshō 14, Hideyoshi sent envoys for a second time. This time, besides Oda Uraku and Takigawa Katsutoshi, who had come before, there was Tomita Sakon Tomonobu. Instead of going directly to Hamamatsu Castle, they first visited Yoshida Castle, held by Sakai Tadatsugu of the hard-line faction. When the news reached Ieyasu in Hamamatsu, he calmly pursed his lips in a smile: At last, what was bound to come had come! They must be bringing yet another difficult demand—but why had the envoys gone first to Yoshida?
